gaps.note: No harness has produced the native code that the shipped Monad validator writes. Every native listing used in cycles 25 to 28 (out/pm-asm-0.16.7.txt and the 913 block coverage table) comes from a clang build of the emitter. The theme-monad-shipped-emitter verifier says so: the MULMOD 2^128 and 2^96 sequences at pc 22378 and 22639 were traced by hand from the clang listing, and the result 'still rests on the clang harness's output standing for the gcc' build. The gcc 15.2.0 emitter's literal arms for shift_by_literal, signextend and byte, and its register and spill bookkeeping, were not lifted (L-1145 and L-1141 inconclusive). Critic query 2026-11-27: rpc.monad.xyz answered Monad/0.16.7 at block 0x77e43a7 (one earlier request got 'Rate limit exceeded').

theme-tempo-release-binary-read lifted the arithmetic, comparison, shift and jump destination code of both shipped v1.19.1 binaries, but not KECCAK256 (built with the asm_keccak and keccak_cache_global features), CALLDATALOAD, MCOPY, TLOAD, TSTORE, SLOAD or SSTORE. The verifier's spot check states that the conclusion does not cover them. CurrencyDelta keys every delta by a keccak of (target, currency) in transient storage (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39), so these handlers carry the settlement logic. The release signature key was not tied to the project, so archive identity rests on the .sha256 files served next to the archives. Critic query 2026-11-27: rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz answered tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu; T14 activates on 8 December.

The OffchainLabs go-ethereum submodule at the rc.9 pin b72783f has not been read for any per-EVM operand or result cache of the kind bor added (core/vm/mulmod_memo.go). established-l1 answered L-1148 for BSC and libevm and wrote that 'Nitro's submodule at b72783f and geth's next release belong to other units and were not read here'; arbitrum-family did not take it up, because the v3.13.0 source is unpublished. The question is open for the build that answers arb1.arbitrum.io and Robinhood Chain.

go-ethereum master and its next release were read by no unit this cycle, although bor, BSC, libevm, Nitro and Celo's op-geth all import its core/vm. OPCODES.md (line 627) says only one geth toolchain has run geth's new generated interpreter loop. Critic query 2026-11-27: ethereum.public.blockpi.network answered Geth/v1.17.9-stable-9dffe6e9/linux-amd64/go1.27.2.

Elysium still answers nitro/vlocal+unknown-unknown/linux-amd64/go1.25.12 (critic query 2026-11-27, block 0xac33d2). F-117 checked Go dead store miscompile shapes in the nitro fork 0e44603 source, not in compiled output. go1.25.12 is a different toolchain from the go1.27.x of the other Nitro builds, and no unit has listed the compiler fixes made between go1.25.12 and the current Go release that touch SSA passes used by core/vm or holiman/uint256.

The celo-reth builds 3cbf835 (v1.0.3, ruint 1.18.0) and 06140ff (v1.0.6 to v1.0.8) have only 4,200 and 3,600 pinned vectors. The verifier saw only 74cc8bb and 7680d6d in 107 calls, so the claim that stakely.io rotates four builds is unconfirmed. The critic's request to celo.api.stakely.io on 2026-11-27 got no HTTP answer (code 000).

No unit worked on Ethereum, the seven OP Stack chains with ETH gas, MegaETH or Arc in cycle 28. Critic queries 2026-11-27 show the builds are unchanged: OP Mainnet op-reth/v0.0.0-dev-unknown, Base reth/v2.5.2-9e380dd base/v1.5.6, Unichain, Ink and Soneium op-reth/v2.10.0-rc.4-65e80332, Zora conduit-op-reth/v2.5.1-8f0ccac, World Chain world-chain/v2.8.2-9596311, MegaETH mega-reth/v2.3.1-4499c42@mnet-ash-rpc-2, Arc 'arc/v1'. The three getFeeGrowthInside borrow scripts that cleared L-1143 on HyperEVM were not sent to MegaETH, which cycle 27 named as the other network whose producer has never run those edges.

The L6 cells of eleven networks were last worked in cycle 24 and the rest in cycle 25 (state/ledger.json cells). BNB Chain Jenner, Polygon Salvador and Tempo T14 all fall on 8 December 2026 and Tempo T15 on 15 December. No cycle 28 unit holds the day-one reruns (L-1032, L-1075, L-1076 and L-545 are open and high).

Arc answers 'arc/v1', which names no build, and OPCODES.md lists 'which release each Arc validator runs' and the code behind both Arc endpoints as uncovered. Arc is a network where the native asset has an ERC-20 face over one PoolManager balance (F-032, F-108), so A3 sits directly on its interpreter's value-call hook (F-125). No unit has read the current arc-node release or arc-reth for changes to that hook or to the instruction table since the reading recorded in Check 4.

Merge into F-116 and add the stakely.io builds to it. F-156 (OP Mainnet) and the Robinhood Chain backend split are the same class on other networks.

titles: theme-stale-sync-in-shared-transactions finding 1: an account that runs another user's ERC-4337 operation from inside its own unlock makes every PoolManager router call of that operation revert with AlreadyUnlocked
F-071: a sync left earlier in a shared transaction makes a later native payment revert for routers that settle value without their own sync
duplicates.note: Both make a victim's frame revert by leaving PoolManager transient state set inside a shared transaction, both need the attacker to hold or place the victim's user operation, and both are low. Keep separate ids if the mechanisms must stay distinct, but cross-reference them and share the precondition text, which the same open question settles (whether pending user operations are readable before inclusion).

L-001: after the announced ArbOS upgrade, how are ElysiumCoreWriter result callbacks delivered and does the upgrade add any system address that moves native HYPE

titles: theme-monad-native-unentered-blocks lead (low): run the 23 multi-transaction scenarios of scen28.py through the gcc-built emitter of the shipped validator package once a harness can link or model it
theme-monad-shipped-emitter lead (medium): run the emitter's register and spill bookkeeping of the gcc build in a model with a stub of asmjit's Assembler
duplicates.note: Both need the same thing, native code produced by the gcc emitter. One work item: build the model, then feed it the PoolManager blocks that scen28.py and the earlier cases enter.

leads.question: Lift the compile-time arithmetic of shift_by_literal for SHL, SHR and SAR (0x372dc0, 0x374090 and the inlined SAR arm), shift_literal_by_non_literal (inlined into shl and shr), and the literal-index arms of signextend (0x388440) and byte (0x37f1f0) from the gcc 15.2.0 disassembly of monad 0.16.7 into the cycle 27 x86 model. Run them on the 142 shift counts, the 5 shifted literals and the indexes 1, 2 and 15 that the PoolManager carries, plus every 64-bit limb boundary. Does each fold give the specified word?
leads.why: TickMath (getSqrtPriceAtTick's shift by 255 and shift by 32), BitMath's BYTE tables, TickBitmap's position and the SIGNEXTEND of Slot0 and BalanceDelta run through these arms in validator native code only. A wrong fold would change mined swap amounts, and eth_call could not show it, so an ordinary swapper could profit from it.

leads.question: Can the gcc build's block_prologue (0x392cd0), write_to_final_stack_offsets (0x3816e0) and the alloc and spill functions be run in the x86 model with a recording stub for asmjit's Assembler, on the 49 PoolManager blocks whose stack depth is largest at entry and exit? Does the recorded instruction stream equal the clang harness listing out/pm-asm-0.16.7.txt for those blocks? Once the model produces gcc-emitted code, also feed it the PoolManager blocks that the 23 scenarios of cycles/028/theme-monad-native-unentered-blocks.work/scripts/scen28.py enter.
leads.why: If the gcc emitter assigns a register or spill slot differently from the clang harness build, every cross-engine comparison of cycles 25 to 28 tested code that validators do not run. A wrong spill in a FullMath or SqrtPriceMath block would change mined amounts.

leads.question: When the Tempo release that carries T14 is posted at download.tempo.xyz/binaries (before 8 December 2026 15:00 UTC), do its Cargo.lock pins of evm2 and ruint differ from 35aa328 and 1.21.1? If they do, rerun the arith_a64.py, arith_x64.py, jd_a64.py and jd_x64.py lifts of cycles/028/theme-tempo-release-binary-read.work on the new x86_64 and aarch64 binaries before activation (L-1075).
leads.why: Tempo has one client, so a fault in the release that activates T14 is the network's answer for every swap. The binary lift method now exists and can be run before the fork rather than after it.

leads.question: In both shipped tempo v1.19.1 binaries, do the KECCAK256 handler (with the asm_keccak and keccak_cache_global code), TLOAD, TSTORE, MCOPY and CALLDATALOAD compute the specified result when lifted into the a64emu and x86 models and run on the battery's KECCAK256 offset and length pairs, the MCOPY overlap cases and a sequence of TSTORE and TLOAD on keccak-derived slots?
leads.why: CurrencyDelta stores each delta at keccak(target, currency) in transient storage (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39), and unlock trusts NonzeroDeltaCount (src/PoolManager.sol:112). A cache or keccak fault that aliased two delta slots would let one account's debt be booked against another's credit.

leads.question: In the gcc-built monad 0.16.7 binary, do the sload and sstore of runtime/storage.cpp, Context::increase_capacity, the keccak wrapper and the tload and tstore paths reached from native code equal the tagged source? Also, does the native GAS value at the three PoolManager CALL sites (src/types/Currency.sol:48 and :73, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134) and at the balanceOf STATICCALL (Currency.sol:94) equal what the interpreter passes, including remaining_block_base_gas, for staticcall as well as call?
leads.why: If native code forwarded different gas to a hook or token than the interpreter, a gas-sensitive callee could succeed in one engine and fail in the other. Validators would then write different PoolManager state than every tracing RPC node.

leads.question: Does go-ethereum master core/vm (instructions.go, interpreter.go, the generated loop and any new cache file) or the OffchainLabs/go-ethereum branch that Nitro master pins hold any operand, result or reciprocal cache of the kind bor added in mulmod_memo.go? Which of bor, BSC, libevm and Nitro already merge that code?
leads.why: bor's memo shows that a geth fork can add caches to the arithmetic path. Five of the 21 networks import geth's core/vm. A cache keyed on fewer bits than the operands would change FullMath.mulDiv results in blocks.

leads.question: Do the three scripts that made each unchecked subtraction of getFeeGrowthInside borrow (cycles/028/hyperevm.work, src/libraries/Pool.sol:498-509 and Position.sol:91-96) return the reference words on mainnet.megaeth.com and in both Monad engines of the repaired harness?
leads.why: Cycle 27 named these borrows as the edges no mined MegaETH or HyperEVM frame had used. They were cleared only on HyperEVM, and a wrong word there would misallocate fees between LPs.

leads.question: Which Go compiler fixes between go1.25.12 and the current Go release touch SSA passes (prove, branchelim, deadstore, the bounds check eliminator) or the math/bits intrinsics that holiman/uint256 uses? Does any affected function shape occur in Nitro's core/vm or in uint256 v1.3.2?
leads.why: Elysium is the only network on go1.25.12, and its build names no source. A miscompile in Mul, MulMod or the shift helpers would change pool math for every Elysium pool.

leads.question: Over 300 three-element web3_clientVersion batches to the stakely.io Celo endpoint the unit used, how often does each of 74cc8bb, 7680d6d, 3cbf835 and 06140ff answer? If 3cbf835 or 06140ff answers, can the full battery and targeted sets be pinned to it?
leads.why: This settles the plausible verdict on the Celo superseded-build finding and the contradiction between the unit (four builds) and its verifier (two builds in 107 calls).

leads.question: Which arc-node and arc-reth release does the Arc endpoint run? Does the frame hook of F-125 or any other instruction override differ in it from the version Check 4 read? Can the battery and set 2 native take cases be pinned to one Arc backend?
leads.why: On Arc the native asset and the USDC face share one PoolManager balance. A change in the value-call hook would change what native takes and face transfers return.

leads.question: F-040's clearance rests on every PoolManager storage write going to a fixed slot below 7 or to a keccak output plus an offset below 7. Is that also true of every write in the deployed Avalanche bytecode? Walk all SSTORE sites in build/PoolManager.json with the jumpmap and confirm that each slot operand comes from KECCAK256 plus a constant or from a constant.
leads.why: The clearance was argued from the source. A bytecode walk would show that no compiler-generated slot arithmetic (packed struct offsets, array indexing) yields slots differing only in bit 248, which Avalanche folds together.
